extracted.intended_audience: Cosmetics industry stakeholders: manufacturers, packers, processors, distributors, facility operators, and responsible persons subject to MoCRA/FDA regulation
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize statutory requirements and FDA-implemented obligations under the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA) that cosmetics industry actors must follow to remain compliant, including reporting, registration, safety substantiation, and manufacturing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse Event (AE) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any health-related event associated with the use of a cosmetic product that is adverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the foundational term for reporting obligations; distinguishes general adverse events from 'serious adverse events' which have additional consequences and reporting timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious Adverse Event (SAE) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An adverse event that (A) results in: death; a life‑threatening experience; inpatient hospitalization; a persistent or significant disability or incapacity; a congenital anomaly or birth defect; an infection; or significant disfigurement (including serious and persistent rashes, second‑ or third‑degree burns, significant hair loss, or persistent or significant alteration of appearance), other than as intended under conditions of use that are customary or usual; or (B) requires, based on reasonable medical judgment, a medical or surgical intervention to prevent an outcome described in (A) above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition determines which events trigger mandatory reporting and possible regulatory actions (e.g., recalls, inspections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse Event Reporting — timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A responsible person is required to report serious adverse events associated with the use of cosmetic products in the United States to FDA within 15 business days. The responsible person must include a copy of the label on or within the retail packaging of such cosmetic product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the responsible person receives medical or other information about the adverse event within 1 year of the initial report to FDA, they must submit this new information to FDA within 15 business days. Reports may be submitted electronically or via paper form. FDA will have access to adverse event reports during an inspection. See FDA resources on how industry reports serious adverse events and the AEMS public dashboard for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory nature of SAE reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: It is mandatory for responsible persons to submit serious adverse event reports for cosmetic products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting cannot be treated as voluntary for SAEs; responsible persons must use the available submission methods (electronic or paper) and follow reporting timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility Registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers and processors must register their facilities with FDA and renew their registration every two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is required for establishments that manufacture or process cosmetic products distributed in the United States; includes importer's establishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA authority to suspend facility registration
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA has the authority to suspend a facility’s registration if the agency determines that a cosmetic product manufactured or processed by the registered facility and distributed in the United States has a reasonable probability of causing serious adverse health consequences or death to humans, and the agency has a reasonable belief that other products manufactured or processed by the facility may be similarly affected because of a failure that cannot be isolated to a product or products, or is sufficiently pervasive to raise concerns about other products manufactured in the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension permits FDA to address pervasive or non‑isolatable failures across a facility rather than a single product problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of registration suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If a facility’s registration is suspended, it is a prohibited act to distribute or sell (or otherwise introduce or deliver into commerce) in the United States cosmetic products from the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension effectively halts legal commerce of products from that facility until registration is reinstated or other remedial steps are taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product Listing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A responsible person must list each marketed cosmetic product with FDA, including product ingredients, and provide any updates annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual updates are required to keep FDA's product listings current; product ingredient disclosure is part of the listing obligation. See FDA's Registration & Listing guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records Access Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If certain conditions are met, FDA can access and copy certain records related to a cosmetic product, including safety records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA has statutory records access authority for cosmetics under MoCRA; the agency has published a Draft Guidance for Industry on FDA Records Access Authority for Cosmetics Products to explain when and how it will exercise this authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Recall Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency determines that there is a reasonable probability that a cosmetic is adulterated or misbranded and the use of or exposure to the cosmetic will cause serious adverse health consequences or death, FDA has the authority to order a mandatory recall if the responsible person refuses to do so voluntarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may use this power after attempting to obtain a voluntary recall; FDA has published Questions and Answers Regarding Mandatory Cosmetics Recalls for additional detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Substantiation records requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A responsible person is required to ensure and maintain records supporting adequate safety substantiation of their cosmetic products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although neither the law nor FDA regulations require specific tests to demonstrate safety, manufacturers may use relevant safety data already available. Data used to support safety should be derived from scientifically robust methods. Animal testing is not required to market a cosmetic product. See FDA resources on product testing of cosmetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA requires FDA to establish regulations for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements for facilities that manufacture cosmetic products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA has held public meetings and issued draft guidance related to Cosmetic Good Manufacturing Practices; final regulatory requirements will detail specific GMP obligations once promulgated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fragrance allergen labeling requirement (to be established)
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA requires FDA to establish fragrance allergen labeling requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA will develop regulatory details specifying how fragrance allergens must be disclosed on product labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized testing methods for asbestos in talc-containing products
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA requires FDA to establish standardized testing methods for detecting and identifying asbestos in talc-containing cosmetic products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA has proposed/withdrawn test-method rulemaking actions (e.g., Proposed Rule December 2024; Withdrawal November 2025) as part of developing these standardized methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS assessment and reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA requires FDA to publish a report summarizing the results of the assessment of the use of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances ("PFAS") in cosmetic products and the scientific evidence regarding the safety of such use, including any associated risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA published 'Report on the Use of PFAS in Cosmetic Products and Associated Risks' on December 29, 2025, summarizing its assessment and evidence regarding safety and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business exemptions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA exempts certain small businesses from GMP, registration, and product listing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions do not apply to manufacturers or facilities that make products that: regularly contact the mucous membrane of the eye; are injected; are intended for internal use; are intended to alter appearance for more than 24 hours (when removal by the consumer is not customary); or to certain products/facilities subject to drug and device requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Person definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The manufacturer, packer, or distributor of a cosmetic product whose name appears on the label of such cosmetic product in accordance with section 609(a) of the FD&C Act or section 4(a) of the Fair Packaging and Labeling Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legal designation determines who carries obligations for reporting, listing, and other MoCRA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any establishment (including an establishment of an importer) that manufactures or processes cosmetic products distributed in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the scope of which physical locations must register and comply with facility-related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted submission methods and transparency tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible persons can submit serious adverse event reports for cosmetic products to FDA using either electronic or paper form submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA provides resources such as 'How to Report a Cosmetic Product Related Complaint' and the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS) Public Dashboard to support submissions and public transparency.
